USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-qa2xb4u3

It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Write tests in test_reduce.py that compare the brute-force solvers in problems.py on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise reduce.py until the tests pass. {"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-qa2xb4u3 && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Reduction
---------
Given a Clique instance  G = (V, E), k  with |V| = n, produce the Vertex
Cover instance on the complement graph  G' = (V, E')  with

        E' = { {u, v} : u != v and {u, v} not in E }
        k' = n - k

Correctness
-----------
A set S of vertices is a clique in G  iff  S is an independent set in the
complement graph G' (every non-edge of G is an edge of G', so a clique of G
has no G' edges inside it, and vice versa).  A set C is a vertex cover of G'
iff V \\ C is an independent set of G'.  Therefore

    G has a clique of size >= k
        iff G' has an independent set of size >= k
        iff G' has a vertex cover of size <= n - k
        iff the produced Vertex Cover instance is a yes-instance.

The construction runs in O(n^2) time, i.e. polynomial in the input size.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

Instance = dict[str, Any]


def reduce(instance: Instance) -> Instance:
    """Reduce a Clique instance to an equivalent Vertex Cover instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Normalise the edge set (undirected, no self loops, no duplicates).
    edges = set()
    for u, v in instance["edges"]:
        if u == v:
            continue
        edges.add((u, v) if u < v else (v, u))

    # Build the complement graph on the same vertex set.
    complement_edges = []
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (u, v) not in edges:
                complement_edges.append([u, v])

    # Clique of size >= k in G  <=>  vertex cover of size <= n - k in G'.
    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
EOF
